newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Iraq Bakr port oil export capacity untested - Saybolt.
newsitem.headline: Iraq Bakr port oil export capacity untested - Saybolt.

text.p: The capacity of Iraq to export oil directly from their southern port of Mina al Bakr will not be known until the first oil is pushed through the system, a spokesman for inspectors Saybolt said on Tuesday.
"We have not done any functional testing. We will have to see. It can only be done once a tanker is waiting," said the spokesman.
The oil flows cannot be tested to the port because there are no storage tanks available. Until a tanker is ready to load, such a test would involve piping oil into the sea.
Pipeline oil flows into storage tanks have already been tested at the Iraqi/Turkish border and at Turkey's Mediterranean terminal at Ceyhan.
"Ceyhan can commence loading at any time," the spokesman said.
Earlier, oil sources in Asia said Iraqi crude was unlikely to hit Asia until January due to problems at Mina al-Bakr.

"The lines and equipment at the terminal are not totally acceptable. Some of the pipelines have rusted and corroded and need to be replaced," said a source close to the U.N. appointed inspectorate from Saybolt.
Asian traders also say that refiners are not able to lift the oil at such short notice.

Iraq's oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said in a statement that Iraq would give preference to Turkey in selling Iraqi oil, but added that oil would start to flow from the southern Iraqi terminal on Friday or Saturday.
